preconditions.description: Grid dimensions n, m and number of queries q are within specified bounds.

preconditions.expression: all(1 <= t <= 3 and 1 <= r1 <= n and 1 <= r2 <= n and 1 <= c1 <= m and 1 <= c2 <= m for t, r1, c1, r2, c2 in queries)
preconditions.description: Each query has a valid type t and coordinates within the grid bounds.

preconditions.expression: all((2 <= r1 <= r2 <= n - 1 and 2 <= c1 <= c2 <= m - 1) if t == 1 else True for t, r1, c1, r2, c2 in queries)
preconditions.description: For type 1 (add barrier), the rectangle is strictly inside the grid boundaries (not touching the outer border).

preconditions.expression: all((2 <= r1 <= r2 <= n - 1 and 2 <= c1 <= c2 <= m - 1) if t == 2 else True for t, r1, c1, r2, c2 in queries)
preconditions.description: For type 2 (remove barrier), the rectangle is strictly inside the grid boundaries.
The problem statement guarantees that barriers do not intersect or share points, and type 2 queries only remove existing barriers.

postconditions.expression: len(output_lines) == len([q for q in queries if q[0] == 3])
postconditions.description: The number of output lines equals the number of type 3 queries.

postconditions.expression: all(line in ['Yes', 'No'] for line in output_lines)
postconditions.description: Each output line is either 'Yes' or 'No'.

postconditions.expression: all((output_lines[i] == 'Yes') == (is_reachable(queries[:i+1], r1, c1, r2, c2)) for i, (t, r1, c1, r2, c2) in enumerate(queries) if t == 3)
postconditions.description: For each type 3 query, the output is 'Yes' if and only if there exists a path from (r1, c1) to (r2, c2) that does not cross any currently active barriers, and 'No' otherwise. The set of active barriers is determined by the sequence of type 1 and type 2 queries preceding the current query.
